newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris, oil firms sign $2 billion Caspian Sea deal.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, oil firms sign $2 billion Caspian Sea deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan and a consortium of foreign oil companies led by Amoco Corp.'s Amoco Eurasian Petroleum Company signed a $2 billion deal Saturday in Baku to develop the Ashrafi and Dan Ulduzu oil fields.
The 25-year contract is Azerbaijan's fourth major deal with a consortium of Western companies, in the Caucasus republic's Caspian Sea reserves.
Amoco said it hopes to sign another exploration agreement with the former Soviet republic soon.
The Western consortium in the latest deal includes Amoco Eurasian, with a 30 percent stake, Unocal with 25.5 percent, Japan's Itochu with 20 percent and Saudi Arabia's Delta Nimir with 4.5 percent.

The Azerbaijan state oil company SOCAR will have a 20 percent stake in the deal and Azeri oil officials say 65 to 80 percent of profits from the development of the fields will go to the Azeri government.

The Ashrafi and Dan Ulduzu fields lie appoximately 30 miles off the Apsheron peninsula. They are spread over 453 square kilometres (175 sqare miles) at depths of 75 to 200 meters (246 to 656 feet) and are estimated to contain 150 million metric tons of crude.
First production is expected to come on line in 2003 and will reach seven million tons per year by 2007.
The deal requires an up-front bonus payment to the Azeri government of $75 million from consortium members and must be ratified by the Azeri parliament.
The deal brings total western investment in Azerbaijan's promising oil sector to over $12 billion.
Azeri President Haydar Aliyev said the agreement was evidence of the growing importance of the former Soviet republic for American companies.
Azerbaijan, with its vast Capsian oil potential, has been the centre of a tug-of-war between Russia, Iran, Trukey and Western countries since independence in 1991.
Tom Stacy, chairman of Amoco Eurasian Petroleum Company, told a news conference that the oil giant hoped to sign another Caspian contract with the Azeri government soon.
